investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the Pending state, meaning the remote agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod remained unscheduled for ~142–145 seconds across all three checks, no VM was allocated, no agent reached a ready state, and the eval runner received an empty evidence object, violating all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) defined in the expected-output contract at infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json line 256.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message ('2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm') and is consistent across all three sibling checks firing within the same ~7-minute window.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's scheduling constraints restrict it to only the 2 kata-capable nodes, and those nodes are full. If the affinity rules were broadened or additional kata-capable nodes were added, scheduling might succeed. The message '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' confirms the remaining nodes are structurally excluded.

Tertiary — cluster capacity not scaled to meet demand: the 6-node cluster may have insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota for concurrent eval probes plus production workloads, indicating a capacity planning gap rather than a transient spike.

Lower confidence — transient burst of concurrent remote-agent workloads temporarily exhausting the resource pool: if other jobs or users were simultaneously consuming kata VM slots, the resource could be transiently exhausted and recover on retry. No traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence to confirm or deny this.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which are fully exhausted, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector requirements. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime with zero evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message all missing).
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity: 0 of 6 nodes could schedule the eval's remote-agent pod. The 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" (resource quota exhausted), and the other 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api runtime environment and is confirmed as an eval-infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: published-observability-snapshot Eval Fail: Snapshot Stale at 720 Minutes (Limit 300)
investigation.summary: The eval for the published-observability-snapshot check failed because the snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json was 720 minutes old at eval time, exceeding the contract's maximum allowed age of 300 minutes. All other public-website sibling checks passed, isolating the failure entirely to the staleness of the published snapshot JSON, not to any broader website or infrastructure outage.
investigation.rootCause: The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for regenerating and publishing the observability snapshot at https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json did not run successfully within the required 300-minute window. The snapshot was 720 minutes old when the eval ran at 2026-07-28T13:02:38.506Z, meaning the last successful publish occurred approximately 12 hours prior.
